Subject: Fidelity security questionnaire — data locality & retention (hosted API)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our standard Security Questionnaire PDF. A couple of focused questions we need clarified for our privacy and legal teams:

1) Can you confirm where request payloads (prompts + metadata) are stored by default for Redwood Hosted API (region/region-fallback behavior)?
2) What are the retention windows for: request payloads, request/response logs, operational logs/metrics, daily snapshots/backups, and any archival backups?
3) How quickly can data be removed upon an account termination or an explicit erase request? Any dependence on cloud provider lifecycles?
4) Do you persist KV caches or prefix caches to disk or object storage, and if so, what is their retention schedule?
5) Are snapshots or backups copied outside the request region (cross-region replication)? If yes, where and for how long?

We primarily care about defaults for hosted API customers and any contractual options for shorter retention. If possible, please attach a short matrix or spreadsheet.

Best,
Alex
Security Architect, Fidelity Analytics

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. I'm looping in Neha and Irene from Security/Privacy; I prepared an initial high-level summary and attached a one-page matrix. Neha will follow up with the operational deletion flow and SLAs.

High-level answers up front:
- Default storage region = the cloud region you select when creating your API key/tenant (we support region pinning). We will fail back to a nearby Redwood region within the same geography if capacity/failover is required; full cross-geo replication is not enabled by default.
- Default retention (hosted API): request payloads & generated outputs kept 30 days; request logs/metrics retained 90 days; daily disaster-recovery snapshots retained 14 days; offsite backups retained 90 days (only for disaster recovery).
- Deletion SLO: live data removed from primary store within 72 hours of a verified erase request; background purge of snapshots/backups within 30 days; final object lifecycle removal may be completed by cloud provider up to 90 days depending on object replication/immutable snapshots.
- KV/prefix caches: primary caches are in-memory / ephemeral by design; we do not persist KV cache contents to long-term object storage for hosted API requests unless a customer opts into a persistent cache feature (contracted).

See attached quick matrix for region-by-region defaults. 

— Soojin
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex — Neha from Security here. Below is an operational, auditor-friendly response you can include in your vendor risk assessment. I've included concrete timelines and notes on exceptions. If you need a signed SOC/Attestation addendum we can route that through Legal.

1) Storage region / locality
- Default behavior: data for Hosted API tenants is stored in the cloud region chosen during tenant provisioning (region pinning). In failover scenarios Redwood will route requests to an alternate region within the same geography (US/EU/APAC) to maintain availability; cross-geo replication is not performed as a default. Cross-region replication and geo-archival are available as a contractual option and would be documented in the SLA.

2) Retention windows (default hosted API plan)
- Request payloads (prompts + metadata) and generated outputs: retained for 30 days from time of ingestion.
- Request/response logs and traces (used for debugging & tracing): retained for 90 days. Aggregated usage metrics for billing and analytics are retained for 24 months.
- In-memory caches (prefix/KV caches): not persisted to durable object storage for standard hosted API usage; caches are volatile and expired based on activity (typical TTLs are minutes to hours).
- Daily disaster-recovery snapshots: retained for 14 days; snapshots are encrypted and stored in the same region by default.
- Offsite backups (cold storage): retained for 90 days (used for longer recovery windows); cold-storage retention beyond 90 days requires contractual agreement.

3) Deletion / erase request flow and timelines
- Customer-initiated erase (self-serve via Console + verified support ticket):
  a) A verified erase request triggers removal from live/primary stores within 72 hours.
  b) Background purge job removes entries from snapshots and offsite backups within 30 calendar days.
  c) Object lifecycle with the underlying cloud provider may cause residual physical copies to be reclaimed as part of the provider's deletion process; customers should expect eventual physical removal within an additional window of up to 60 days in worst-case scenarios. In total worst-case end-to-end: 90 days from verified request for full physical object deletion.
- Emergency or compliance deletions: Redwood will prioritize contractual emergency deletions and can engage our legal/compliance teams for expedited timelines subject to attestations and signed addenda.

4) Encryption / KMS
- All data at rest and in transit is encrypted. By default Redwood manages encryption keys. For customers who require it, we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via integrations with major KMS providers; snapshots and backups can be encrypted with the customer's CMK when CMK is enabled for the tenant.

5) Cross-region replicas and snapshot copies
- Default: no cross-geo replication of customer data. Snapshots and backups remain in the selected region unless cross-region replication is contractually enabled. If replication is enabled, Redwood documents all replica locations and retention windows in the customer SLA.

6) Audit evidence and escalation contacts
- Evidence: Redwood can provide (1) a retention & deletion matrix (spreadsheet), (2) sample S3/object storage lifecycle policies, (3) sample deletion logs from completed erase requests (redacted), and (4) SOC 2 report under NDA.
- Escalation: security@redwood.ai is primary; for urgent compliance escalations contact Neha Kapoor (neha_kapoor@redwood.ai) and Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.ai).

Summary paragraph for vendor risk assessment (copyable):
"Redwood Inference (Hosted API) stores customer request payloads and generated outputs in the cloud region selected at tenant provision. By default, request payloads and outputs are retained for 30 days, request/response logs for 90 days, daily DR snapshots for 14 days, and offsite backups for 90 days. Live data removal from primary stores is completed within 72 hours of a verified erase request, with background purges of snapshots/backups completed within 30 days. Final physical deletion from the underlying cloud provider may take up to 90 days end-to-end. Customers requiring shorter retention, cross-region replication, or use of customer-managed keys can contractually enable those options. For evidence and attestation, contact security@redwood.ai."

If you want, I can also produce a one-page signed attestation and a short timeline graphic for your audit pack — happy to help.
